subject: Numeracy
title: Money in the market
objectives: Children will recognise Nigerian coins and notes in play.
Children will buy items with play money.
content: Coins and notes, buying with play money, and giving change with objects.
teachingActivities: Use play coins and notes or school-made tokens that look like Nigerian naira; never use real money with children at this age; keep prices to small numbers (1 to 10 play naira); link to market and tuck-shop experiences; respect that families have different incomes and never ask about money at home.
learnerActivities: Name coins and notes used in play and buy one item with play money.
resources: A play market stall with toy goods
assessment: Observe whether each child names play coins and notes and buys one item with play money.
expectedOutcomes: Names coins and notes used in play.
Buys one item with play money.
crossCurricular: Social Habits: manners at the market
Understanding the World: shops and markets

lessons.title: Coins and notes
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will look at play coins and notes and say that we use money to buy things.
successCriteria: Names a coin and a note
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count to 20, add and take away to 5 and read a simple graph.
lessons.starter: Show a play coin and say "This is a coin. We use money to buy things at the market."
teacherActivities: Show a coin and a note and say their names.
Let children hold and feel the play money.
Say "Coins are round and notes are flat."
Sort the play money into coins and notes.
learnerActivities: Children look and repeat the names.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show a coin and a note and say their names. Children: Children look and repeat the names.
Step 2. Teacher: Let children hold and feel the play money. Children: Children touch coins and notes.
Step 3. Teacher: Say "Coins are round and notes are flat." Children: Children repeat the sentence.
Step 4. Teacher: Sort the play money into coins and notes. Children: Child sorts coins and notes.

practical.title: Sort the money
steps: Put coins and notes in separate piles.
practical.safety: Use large play coins that cannot be swallowed and never use real money. Supervise closely and keep coins out of mouths.

differentiation.support: Sort two kinds of play money.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say what the money can buy.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we use to buy things?
Is this a coin or a note?

expectedOutcomes: Names a coin and a note
lessons.conclusion: Put the money away and say coin and note.
lessons.homeConnection: Talk about why we use money when you shop.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "look at play coins and notes and say that we use money to buy things" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Buying with play money
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will buy one item at a play market using play money.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count to 20, add and take away to 5 and read a simple graph.
resources: Toy fruit with price labels of 1 to 5
lessons.starter: Set up a market stall and say "We are going shopping. Each thing costs some money."
teacherActivities: Show how to choose an item and read its price.
Show how to count out the coins to pay.
Let each child buy an item.
Remind children to say please and thank you.
learnerActivities: Child pays and takes the item.
Child says please and thank you.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to choose an item and read its price. Children: Children watch.
Step 2. Teacher: Show how to count out the coins to pay. Children: Children count along.
Step 3. Teacher: Let each child buy an item. Children: Child pays and takes the item.
Step 4. Teacher: Remind children to say please and thank you. Children: Child says please and thank you.

practical.title: Play market
practical.safety: Use only play money and toy goods and supervise closely. Keep the stall area clear.

differentiation.support: Buy items that cost one or two.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to buy two items and count the cost.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Buys an item with play money
lessons.conclusion: Tidy the stall and say thank you.
lessons.homeConnection: Play a market game with play money at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "buy one item at a play market using play money" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Being the seller
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will act as the seller and take payment and give an item.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count to 20, add and take away to 5 and read a simple graph.
lessons.starter: Say "Now some of you are sellers. The seller says the price and takes the money."
teacherActivities: Show how the seller says the price.
Let seller children count the coins they receive.
Give the item to the buyer.
Swap the buyer and seller roles.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how the seller says the price. Children: Children watch.
Step 2. Teacher: Let seller children count the coins they receive. Children: Seller counts the coins.
Step 3. Teacher: Give the item to the buyer. Children: Seller hands over the item.
Step 4. Teacher: Swap the buyer and seller roles. Children: Child swaps and buys.

practical.title: Market sellers
practical.safety: Use only play money and keep the area orderly. Supervise swapping of roles.

differentiation.extension: Ask the seller to give change with objects.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Tidy the stall and say thank you.
lessons.homeConnection: Play shopkeeper at home with a friend.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "act as the seller and take payment and give an item" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Giving change
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will use counters to show how change is given.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count to 20, add and take away to 5 and read a simple graph.
lessons.starter: Say "I have five coins. The apple costs three. How many do I have left?"
teacherActivities: Pay three coins from five and count what is left.
Let children pay with more coins and find the change.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Pay three coins from five and count what is left. Children: Children count the change.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "That is the change." Children: Children repeat change.
Step 3. Teacher: Let children pay with more coins and find the change. Children: Child pays and counts change.
Step 4. Teacher: Check by counting all. Children: Child counts all the coins.

practical.title: Change with counters
practical.safety: Use large play coins only and keep totals small. Supervise closely.

differentiation.support: Use totals to three and pay with two coins.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to pay with five and get change from items costing up to four.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Put the coins away and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Play a pretend shop with coins and change.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "use counters to show how change is given" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 7 money check
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child uses play money.
successCriteria: Buys an item with play money
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count to 20, add and take away to 5 and read a simple graph.
lessons.starter: Sing the market song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: sorting money, buying and selling.
At each station ask "How much?" and watch.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: sorting money, buying and selling. Children: Children rotate every five minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "How much?" and watch. Children: Child answers and counts.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Money stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and use play money only. Keep floors clear.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use one coin items.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to buy two items and find the change.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: names coins and notes; pays for an item; acts as seller; finds change with counters.

questions.question: What do we use to buy?

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 7
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say well done.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child uses play money" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
